issue.description:
ADR-002 removes all cross-tool import and makes agent-guided rehydration the only migration path, requiring a reconciliation report that maps every source identifier to a native identifier or an explicit omitted/merged/unresolved disposition and records the source repository and commit. No report schema, template, or validation exists and no bead covers producing one; the ADR itself flags that large repositories need batching, resumable reports, and duplicate detection. Work: specify the report format under docs/ or research/specs/ (per-item dispositions, source repo and commit, review sign-off), and optionally add a validation command so completed rehydrations are reviewable and partially-finished ones are resumable.

---
Priority: P3
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Define the agent-guided rehydration reconciliation report format

issue.description:
## Outcome
`bead init` run in a directory below an existing bead-rs workspace creates a
new workspace rooted at the current directory, as its help text promises
("Initialize a new bead workspace in the current directory"). It no longer
reports "Workspace already exists at: <ancestor>" and quietly hands the
ancestor's store to every later command. Goal: Profile. This is step 4 of the
public NEEDLE README quickstart (`cd <your-repo> && ... bead init --prefix <name>`),
which strangers run against the public bead-rs release.

Work on this issue directly. Do not create sub-issues, do not split this work,
and do not decompose it into smaller tasks.

## Current state (evidence)
Observed 2026-10-26 with the published bead 0.2.6 during a NEEDLE stranger
test. The project was a fresh `git init` repo at
`/home/coding/scratch/needle-stranger.X/proj`, and `/home/coding/scratch/.beads`
already existed (a smoke-test store):

    $ bead init --prefix quickstart
    Workspace already exists at: /data/build/scratch
    Prefix: bead
    UUID: 21a9e91e-...
    Schema up to date (version 22)          # exit 0
    $ bead create --title 'Add a CONTRIBUTING.md ...' --priority 2
    bead-fbc07f04                           # written into the ancestor's store

The requested prefix was ignored, migrations ran against the ancestor's
database, and the bead landed in an unrelated workspace (bead-fbc07f04 was
closed afterwards as a test artifact).

Cause, at origin/main dd79a2d0: `cmd_init` (src/main.rs ~1320) calls
`store::WorkspaceConfig::probe()` (src/store/mod.rs:156-188). probe walks up
from cwd and returns `Ready` for the first ancestor `.beads/config.json`, and
`cmd_init` treats `Ready` as "already exists".

## Scoped work
- `cmd_init`: when probe finds a `Ready` workspace whose root is not the
  current directory, initialize a new workspace at the current directory
  (same code path as `NotFound`). Keep today's behaviour unchanged when the
  root is the current directory (idempotent re-init, pending migrations).
- Keep the R030 refusal for a foreign `.beads` in the current directory.
- Add a test in tests/cli_init.rs that creates an outer workspace, runs
  `bead init --prefix inner` in a nested directory, and asserts: a new
  `.beads/config.json` exists in the nested directory with prefix `inner`,
  stderr names the nested root, and the outer store's issue count is
  unchanged.

## Acceptance (a worker can run these)
- `cargo test --test cli_init` passes, including the new nested-init test.
- `cargo check --all-targets --quiet` (the workspace gate) passes.
- Throwaway check: `T=$(mktemp -d /tmp/b1.XXXXXX); (cd "$T" && bead init --prefix outer) && mkdir "$T/inner" && (cd "$T/inner" && <built bead> init --prefix inner)`
  prints `Root: $T/inner`, and `ls "$T/inner/.beads/config.json"` exists;
  `rm -rf "$T"`.
- Pushed commit on main of jedarden/bead-rs (Forgejo origin).

## Out of scope
- Changing discovery for any command other than `init`.
- The `--skip-foreign-workspace` semantics.
- Cutting a bead-rs release.
issue.title: bead init in a directory below an existing workspace creates a new workspace there instead of adopting the ancestor, so that cargo test --test cli_init passes. Work on this issue directly.

issue.description:
Two symptoms, one feature area, both reproducible on main as of 154e3d3+dee7123 (verified with sources stashed to pristine HEAD):

1. tests/r028_fork_identity.rs — 5 failures (8 pass): test_fork_creates_fork_receipt, test_fork_creates_summary_event, test_fork_never_implicit_or_inferred, test_fork_requires_checkpoint, test_fork_requires_clean_checkpoint. In-process calls die with `UNIQUE constraint failed: events.sequence` (the fork summary event reuses a live sequence), and test_fork_requires_checkpoint expects an error that no longer fires.

2. tests/mutating_command_event_contract.rs::every_mutating_command_advances_the_live_event_sequence fails at `bead sync reconcile`: the covered-ahead qualifier "valid staged stream" (src/service/reconcile.rs:216 -> checkpoint.rs:2716 -> validate_event_sequence, checkpoint.rs:2930) demands every origin's first staged event have origin_event_sequence == 1, but an R028 fork origin (e.g. <uuid>-fork-52-<hash>) legitimately starts at the fork point (53). reconcile therefore fails closed on any cloned workspace's checkpoint, while the fork workspace's own publication path accepts the same stream — the two paths disagree.

Design fork to resolve (pick one, record in the R027/R028 specs):
- validate_event_sequence accepts a fork origin starting at its recorded fork point (check against the fork identity, not 1), or
- R028 records origin_event_sequence restarting at 1 per origin, or
- reconcile treats fork-origin streams under a separate qualifier.

Repro: TMPDIR=/var/tmp/<clean> cargo test --no-fail-fast --test r028_fork_identity --test mutating_command_event_contract

Refs: research/specs/remote-advanced-reconcile-v1.md; commit acd165d (R028); commit 154e3d3 (swept the contract-test extension that exposed this). Filed from beadrs-e854d52a (R033) whose full-suite gate surfaced the cluster.
issue.title: R028 fork identity breaks sync reconcile and its own conformance tests
